text:
anna: Heads-up, filing follow-up on the gateway <-> edge handoff for streaming retries. Observations + Qs.

mike: TL;DR: we need a compact handshake token in headers so edge can resume mid-stream without reprocessing wide prefixes.

raj: +1 on a small resume token. Needs to include model req id, last-seq, checksum.

sara: checksum might be heavy if we do it per-chunk. Can we use rolling hash? or an incrementing chunk-id with durable kvcache refs?

anna: idea: token = base64({req_id, kvcache_id, last_token_index, fallback_model}), signed by gateway key. No chunk-level checksum.

mike: signed token avoids spoofing across tenants. But how do we handle non-idempotent user ops? we should avoid resuming for side-effecting requests.

raj: we detect side-effects via header `X-Has-Side-Effects: true` set by runtime after pre-flight. If true -> no resume, only failover to fallback model with restart.

sara: runtime can't always know semantic side-effects. Suggest conservative default: flag only when we see 'function_call' or 'tool_call' in the prompt envelope.

anna: ok. Also UX: tracer should show resume vs restart as separate spans. Need explicit trailer `grpc-trailer: resume-applied=true` when resume happens.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-04-01 planned: gateway/edge-handshake-v1 rollouts

mike: perf note: resume tokens need to be tiny to avoid header bloat. Keep <200bytes. Do not include full prompt or model context.

raj: ops question: billing—if resume replays tokens, who absorbs cost? edge should bill for tokens actually served; gateway should mark retries in trace.

sara: proposed next step: RFC PR with handshake proto, header names, token schema + rejection codes. Anyone volunteer to author?

anna: I'll draft the RFC. ping me for review. thanks :v:
